symptoms: The message names a class that the build did resolve, so the code compiled against it
The first occurrence sometimes names a class the job never references directly
Retrying the same job produces the same failure at the same point
likely_causes: The class was present at compile time and is absent at runtime
The static initializer of the class threw, and every later reference reports the class as missing
A transitive dependency of a shipped jar was not shipped with it
diagnostic_steps: Look for an earlier ExceptionInInitializerError in the same log: when it is there, the class is present and its initializer failed, which is a different problem
Compare the jars delivered to the runtime with the dependencies the build resolved, including transitive ones
Check whether the named class belongs to a transitive dependency of a jar that was shipped alone
fixes: Ship the transitive dependency alongside the jar that needs it, or build a shaded artifact that contains it
If an initializer failed, fix that failure: the missing-class message is a consequence, and adding the jar again changes nothing
unsafe_fixes: Treating it as a missing jar without reading the log for an earlier initializer failure, which sends the operator hunting for a jar that is already there
verification: Re-run the job and exercise the code path that loads the class; if an initializer was at fault, confirm the initializer completes
rollback: Revert the classpath change; partial output from the failed run has to be handled separately
